inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $2.06 grown about 31%, close to the consensus FY26-to-FY27 growth (+36%, $1.52 to $2.06) with a little fade. Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 and the $0.38 Q3 guide [3] already annualize to about $1.60, which supports the trajectory.

Set above NVDA (28x) and TSMC's 10-year average (about 23x) [4] because Intel's EPS is growing off a depressed base and supply is constrained. It is well below today's 58-62x FY27 [4][1]. Intel's own history (P/S 1.5-12.5x over a decade [5]) shows peak multiples do not last, and the 2000 peak at about 50x EPS was followed by an 82% drawdown [19].

Consensus EPS is on roughly 5.40B diluted shares (5,285M basic after the full greenshoe [6][22] plus 119M RSUs/PSUs). I add about 50M of the 143M DoC escrow shares, which are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive [22]. That is a ~1% haircut. The phantom ~$15B follow-on I counted in round 1 is removed.

agents.reasoning: Round-2 revision. I verified the supervisor's main correction in the primary filings. There is no planned ~$15B follow-on: $15B was the proposed size of the August deal [23], which was upsized to $20B [24], and the 31.6M-share greenshoe was exercised on Aug 11 [6]. That leaves 5,285M basic shares and $22.62B net proceeds [22], and EDGAR shows no later offering filing [25]. The 424B5 also lists $15.6B of NCI and 143M escrow shares [22], which I had left out. Net effect on fair value: removing the phantom dilution helps, while the NCI, the higher H2 net debt and the escrow shares hurt, so fair value goes from $99 to $96. Starting point is unchanged: INTC is $120 after +258% in a year and +34% in September, at about 58x FY27 consensus EPS of $2.06 and about 11x sales, near the top of its decade P/S range [1][2][4][5]. Base rates (own computation, 28 large semis/tech names [17]): after a +150% trailing year the median next-12-month return was +48% (n=243), or +25% for the post-2002 ex-mega-winner subset (n=72), with a log SD of 0.63-0.82 and about 19% of cases losing more than 30%. Survivorship bias is heavy, so I cut the momentum drift to about 0-10%. Valuation pulls the other way: fair value of about $96 is 20% below spot, and Intel's 2000 peak at about 50x was followed by -82% [19]. Sell-side consensus of about $116, with 32 of 48 at Hold [1][10], agrees with a flat-to-down center. Manifold's 41% on touching $150 by end-2026 [15] is a bit below a driftless touch model (~55%). Per the source review, I now give no weight to the thin 2027 Polymarket markets (~$10k volume) [11][13]. That removes a little of the bear tail I had attributed to macro. Removing the supply overhang of a phantom follow-on is a small positive for the 12-month path. Together these move my median from $112 to $113. I keep sigma at 0.65 (between the base-rate sample's 0.63-0.82 and slightly below the 76% realized vol, since vol mean-reverts after spikes). Result: P(>=120) is 46%, P(>=60) is 84%, and P(>=300) is 7%. The scenario mean (0.25x$60 + 0.5x$110 + 0.25x$185 = $116) is consistent. I agree with the supervisor's factual corrections. I keep my own ladder rather than the forecaster mean because my base-rate evidence still argues for fatter tails on both sides. Research limits: round-1 data constraints (Twelve Data paywall, Alpha Vantage rate limit) still apply, and round 2 used 7 targeted fetches (EDGAR, 424B5, 8-K, Intel IR).

disagreements.topic: Further equity issuance: is a ~$15B follow-on 'planned'?
disagreements.resolution: No such plan exists. $15B was the original proposed size of the August offering. It was upsized to $20B (210.5M shares at $95), and the 31.6M-share greenshoe was exercised in full, so 242.1M shares and about $23B gross ($22.62B net) were issued. EDGAR shows no new offering filing since 2026-08-12. Some real dilution risk remains: Intel's own lock-up ends at the earlier of 90 days after the prospectus (about Nov 8) or the Q3 earnings release, and the S-3ASR shelf stays open. So a new raise is possible after Oct 22, but nothing has been announced.

disagreements.topic: Share count and claims ahead of common equity
disagreements.resolution: The 424B5 gives 5,285M basic shares after the greenshoe. Adding 119M unvested RSUs/PSUs gives about 5.40B diluted, plus 143M escrowed DoC shares that are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive (about 5.55B fully counted). The 241M warrants are contingent on Intel's foundry ownership falling below 51% and are excluded. NCI was $15.6B at 2026-06-27 per the 424B5 capitalization table, and an equity valuation must deduct it. Pro forma cash plus ST investments is about $52.3B against $50.5B of debt before H2 burn. The corrections cut agent_2's and agent_4's SOTP values by about $3/share and agent_3's by about $1/share.

disagreements.topic: 14A schedule: slip to 2029 volume, or on track?
disagreements.resolution: agent_4's claim is stale. The SemiAnalysis X post (Feb 2026) referred to a Cisco AI Summit remark. On the 2026-07-23 Q2 call, the CEO said Intel remains on track for 14A risk production of internal products in H2 2027, with a commit to high-volume ramp in 2028. That timeline still depends on an external anchor customer, which none of the agents disputes.

disagreements.topic: Apple foundry deal: firm or preliminary?
disagreements.resolution: The deal is still preliminary. WSJ (2026-05-08) and Kuo report that Apple will make its lowest-end M-series chip on 18A-P at Fab 52, with first shipments Q2-Q3 2027, but neither company has officially confirmed it and TSMC keeps more than 90% of Apple's supply. Intel's own disclosure is about $293M a quarter of external foundry revenue. The evidence supports agents 3 and 4 ($110-120B) over agent_2's $200B, but this settles a valuation input, not the direction of the price.

Unresolved at the primary level. Both figures are sell-side numbers relayed through social and forum posts. The 50% figure is the older one, and management says yields are improving about 7-8% a month and reach industry-standard levels in 2027. I give neither figure weight in the ladder.
